html:
Upton Sinclair was an American novelist and political activist, born in 1878 in Baltimore and active until his death in 1968. He is best known for The Jungle, his 1906 novel on the meatpacking industry in Chicago.

A committed socialist, he wrote the book to expose the plight of immigrant workers. The public was struck by its descriptions of unsanitary food, and the outcry helped pass the Pure Food and Drug Act under President Theodore Roosevelt. He wrote dozens of later books and novels, won a Pulitzer Prize in 1943, and ran for governor of California in 1934 on a campaign to "End Poverty in California".
